resolution_summary: B2N's authoritative purpose is formally narrowed to BOUNDED_MIGRATION_LINEAGE_QUALIFICATION, matching exactly what the qualified 1-request/member MigrationGetTransactionAdapter can prove. Full creator-funding evidence acquisition is NOT deleted from the programme -- it is rebound to the existing canonical B2Z contract (already present in this repository as OIP_v2.2E.2B2Z.v1 / src/acquisition/b2z_execution_boundary.py / the 2B2Z preflight family), which remains a separate, non-executable, non-authorized future stage.

b2n_must_prove_per_member: exact mint/member identity (bound to the frozen 20-member manifest, ordinal 1-20)
exact reviewed migration provenance (bound to the P2E reviewed_migration_origin per member)
exact migration transaction lookup/binding (one getTransaction call against the reviewed migration_signature)
transaction/member consistency (the mint appears in the fetched transaction's account keys)
bounded provider execution (<=1 physical request per member, <=20 total)
deterministic attempt accounting (B2NAttemptLedger, append-only, one entry per ordinal)
candidate evidence output (migration-lineage evidence only; no creator-funding claim)
part1_b2n_authoritative_purpose.explicit_non_goal: B2N does not resolve a creator address, does not call getSignaturesForAddress, does not verify an inbound SOL funding transfer, and does not set any field meaning creator-funding evidence to true. This was true of the qualified MigrationGetTransactionAdapter implementation from the start; this reconciliation makes it the DECLARED contract rather than an unstated implementation detail that conflicted with the .md design doc's success criteria.

part2_creator_funding_requirement_preser.note: B2Z already exists as a named, qualified, tested contract in this repository (test_full_fake_run_is_exactly_60_ordered_attempts). This reconciliation does not invent a new B2CF milestone name; B2Z is reused as the canonical creator-funding evidence stage per repository convention.
part2_creator_funding_requirement_preser.b2z_authorization_status_after_this_reco: STILL NOT AUTHORIZED. This artifact does not grant B2Z execution authority. See part7 below.

part3_b2n_success_criteria.field_naming_rationale: Distinct from the shared 'evidence_observed' field name used generically in OneRequestResponse/B2NExecutor plumbing (kept for backward wire-compatibility with existing tests) and from B2Z's evidence_observed=True (creator-funding meaning). This new field is B2N-output-specific and never conflated with B2Z's semantics.
per_member_success_requires_all_of: member/mint bound to the exact frozen 20-member manifest (ordinal, mint, census_event_id match)
reviewed provenance valid (P2E human_approval_decision_record.decision == APPROVED, bound to reviewed_provenance_digest)
migration transaction request succeeded (request_outcome == SUCCESS) OR a valid CACHE_HIT (request_count == 0)
transaction response is well-formed (result is a dict; accountKeys list is present and parseable)

expected migration/mint relationship observed: the member's mint appears in the fetched transaction's account keys, exactly as MigrationGetTransactionAdapter.acquire_once() already checks (mint not in addresses -> MALFORMED_RESPONSE)
provenance/output digest valid (provider_signature returned matches the reviewed migration_signature bound at P2E)
ledger entry reconciles (append-only, no duplicate ordinal, required fields present)
no forbidden authority exercised (no production write, no existing-operation mutation, no retry/pagination/fallback)
part3_b2n_success_criteria.explicit_exclusion: migration_lineage_evidence_observed=true NEVER implies or claims creator_funding_evidence. Any downstream consumer must not conflate the two.

contradiction_found_in.old_text_meaning: evidence_observed was defined as creator-funding evidence, and success criterion 3 required evidence_observed=true from all 20 members -- unsatisfiable by the qualified 1-request adapter
contradiction_found_in.reconciliation_action: This design .md is NOT edited/overwritten by this artifact (it is historical/immutable per repository convention). Instead, this reconciliation artifact is the authoritative CURRENT statement of B2N's narrowed purpose and supersedes the .md's success-criteria section for B2N's actual operating contract. The .md remains valid architectural context explaining WHY a bounded budget was chosen and WHAT the wider ambition was; it is not deleted or silently rewritten.

contradiction_found_in.location: src/acquisition/b2n_qualification.py OneRequestResponse.evidence_observed and B2NExecutor.run() stop condition (line 249)
contradiction_found_in.old_meaning_conflict: The generic field name evidence_observed is shared plumbing between B2N and (conceptually) any future adapter; it does not itself claim creator-funding meaning -- that meaning was only asserted in the .md design doc and never actually reconciled against the concrete adapter's behavior.
contradiction_found_in.reconciliation_action: NOT renamed globally (this field is shared executor/response plumbing, not B2N-exclusive, and a global rename risks breaking B2Z-adjacent semantics per explicit instruction). Instead, B2N's own success determination for reporting/gating purposes uses the new B2N-specific derived field migration_lineage_evidence_observed (see part3), computed FROM but not IDENTICAL TO the generic evidence_observed plumbing field. No code change was required to b2n_qualification.py itself for this reconciliation -- the existing MigrationGetTransactionAdapter behavior (evidence_observed=False, provenance_complete=True, error_class=B2W_MIGRATION_LINEAGE_ONLY) is now the CORRECT and EXPECTED B2N outcome, not a contradiction, once success is measured by migration_lineage_evidence_observed rather than the generic evidence_observed field.

part4_contradiction_removal.code_changes_reason: The qualified implementation (MigrationGetTransactionAdapter, B2NExecutor) already behaves exactly as BOUNDED_MIGRATION_LINEAGE_QUALIFICATION requires. The contradiction was entirely in the .md design doc's stated success criteria referencing a stronger claim (creator-funding evidence) than the bounded 1-request implementation could ever produce. Reconciliation is therefore a CONTRACT/DOCUMENTATION-LEVEL correction, not a code change, consistent with instruction 4's requirement not to weaken or ambiguously rewrite code merely to make an existing implementation pass.

part5_migration_get_transaction_adapter_.exact_input: reviewed migration_signature per member, sourced from B2WInputProjection.from_census() which validates signature/mint/subscription lineage against the frozen manifest before binding
exact_response_requirements: response is a dict with no 'error' key set to non-null (otherwise RPC_ERROR)
response['result'] is a dict (otherwise MALFORMED_RESPONSE, error_class=B2W_RESULT_MISSING)
result['transaction']['message']['accountKeys'] is present and contains the member's mint as a pubkey (otherwise MALFORMED_RESPONSE, error_class=B2W_MINT_NOT_IN_TRANSACTION)
part5_migration_get_transaction_adapter_.evidence_extracted: migration transaction slot (provider_slot), migration_signature echoed back (provider_signature), confirmation that mint appears in the transaction's account keys
part5_migration_get_transaction_adapter_.cache_hit_behavior: Not implemented in MigrationGetTransactionAdapter itself (it always issues exactly one request); cache-hit semantics are handled at the B2NExecutor/OneRequestResponse layer generically (request_count=0, outcome=CACHE_HIT) if a caller supplies a caching-aware client -- MigrationGetTransactionAdapter as committed is not itself a caching client.

failure_semantics.unknown_mint: raises ValueError B2W_MINT_NOT_IN_FROZEN_PROJECTION before any request is issued (zero physical requests)
failure_semantics.success: OneRequestResponse(outcome=SUCCESS, evidence_observed=False, provenance_complete=True, provider_signature=<sig>, provider_slot=<slot>, error_class=B2W_MIGRATION_LINEAGE_ONLY)

part5_migration_get_transaction_adapter_.proof: MigrationGetTransactionAdapter.acquire_once() calls self.transport.post_json() exactly once per invocation; no loop, no retry, no secondary call anywhere in the method body.
